description: Five ways to run ulams: Claude Code, Claude with the ulams MCP server, the ulams command line, the REST API and SDK, and the studio.
footnote: The ulams CLI and MCP server are being built. The commands and tool names shown for them are the planned interface and may change; the REST API and the studio work today.

tabs.label: Claude Code
tabs.title: claude · ~/oncall-academy
tabs.caption: Describe the course in plain language. Claude Code runs the ulams CLI, shows you the outline, and publishes only after you approve.
tabs.note: Planned interface: the ulams CLI is being built (Phase 7). Commands are shown as designed and may change.

lines.text: Build a 3-lesson course on incident response from ./runbook.md and publish it to oncall
I'll start a builder run on runbook.md and bring you the outline before anything goes live.
Outline ready: 1. Detect and declare, 2. Triage and mitigate, 3. Write the postmortem. Every lesson cites runbook.md. Approve and publish?
Done. Incident response is live on oncall: 3 lessons, 9 topics, every claim cited to runbook.md.

tabs.label: Claude + MCP
tabs.title: Claude · ulams MCP server
tabs.caption: Ask Claude, or any MCP-compatible agent, about your academy. It uses the ulams MCP server and asks before it sends anything.
tabs.note: Planned interface: the ulams MCP server is being built (Phase 7). The at-risk report depends on learner analytics (Phase 4), which is not built yet.

lines.text: Which learners are stuck in On-Call this week? Nudge them.
Four learners have not moved in 7 days, all on lesson 2, Triage and mitigate. I can send each a short reminder with a link back to the lesson. Send it?
Done. Four reminders are on their way.

tabs.label: CLI
tabs.title: zsh · ~/academy
tabs.caption: Course as code: pull a course to Markdown, edit it in your editor, review the diff, push it back.
tabs.note: Planned interface: the ulams CLI is being built (Phase 7). Commands are shown as designed and may change.

Use a medium grind for every method.
Match the grind to the method: coarse for French press, fine for espresso.
1 changed, 0 added, 0 removed (dry run, nothing written)

tabs.label: REST & SDK
tabs.title: zsh · api
tabs.caption: Everything the studio does goes through the HTTP API. Plain curl works; so does @ulams/sdk for reading.

lines.text: node -e "import('@ulams/sdk').then(async ({createClient}) => { const ulams = createClient({baseUrl: 'https://oncall.example.com'}); console.log((await ulams.courses.list()).data.length) })"

tabs.label: Studio
tabs.title: Studio · Course builder
tabs.caption: The classic experience is still here: a chat-driven studio where every AI change is a diff you approve.

lines.text: Add a quiz after lesson 2 from the runbook.
